head: 2d6962c38bb21d4cc59f8ccf1efb5911c9d1a1c8
summary:
Attempt 39 fixes B1 at the default window size and above, but not on short windows, which the window allows. One major finding, M1.

I read the whole diff e19dc94..2d6962c and followed it into the files around it:
- MainWindow.xaml: OutcomePanel and TopLevelPanel are now the two rows of one Grid, the window's last child. The outcome row is Auto, or 2* with a 316/328 px floor while visible; the results row is Auto, or 1* while visible. OutcomePanel is aligned to the top, and both outcome lists have MinHeight 24.
- WindowReport.cs gains the additive keys TopLevelPanel and TopLevelList.
- StartupHook.cs accepts FSA_HOOK_EXPAND=1 for watch mode, and the watch line gains listHeight.
- WindowCases.ps1 adds B-007 and a TopLevelList check in B-003.
- docs/design/SL-039-live-results.md describes the shared Grid.

What I ran:
- WindowCases -Case All: all 25 non-network cases pass. B-007 shows TopLevelList 31.26 px closed and 19.26 px opened, and 167.5 px mid-scan.
- HookCases H-001 and H-002: pass.
- Core tests: 181 of 181 pass.
- rules-parity: AGREE.
- Fitness: all 29 rules hold.

My own measurements, from the report on a tree of 6 folders × 25 files, the B1 shape:

| Window | TopLevelList | In view |
|---|---|---|
| 880x600 | 31.26 px | yes |
| 880x1040 | 237.1 px | yes |
| 880x400 | 0 px | no |

So B1 is fixed at 880x600 and above. At 880x400, the window's own MinHeight, TopLevelPanel is 0 px and LargestFilesList is not in view either. The fixed 316 px outcome floor starves the results list on short windows. That is the outcome the B1 disposition chose the shared Grid to avoid, and the new XAML comment says "neither panel can push the other off the window". Nothing runs below 880x600. That is M1.

Every other departure is declared: the 2:1 split with floors instead of equal stars, MinHeight 24, top alignment, and the hook's FSA_HOOK_EXPAND.

findings.claim: On short windows, which the window allows (MinHeight 400, MainWindow.xaml:5), the outcome row's fixed floor pushes SL-039's results list off the window again, and the outcome's own list runs past the bottom. The floor is MinHeight 316, or 328 while the unreadable list is open (MainWindow.xaml:55, :63). I measured the published exe with a throwaway startup hook that only sets Window.Height (now deleted), reading the report's own keys, on a tree of 6 top-level folders × 25 non-empty files. At 880x400: OutcomePanel 300 px, LargestFilesList inView false, TopLevelPanel 0 px, TopLevelList 0 px and not in view. At 880x600: TopLevelList 31.26 px and in view. At 880x1040: TopLevelList 237.1 px. So O-025 holds from about the default height up and fails below roughly 550 px. That is the outcome the B1 disposition picked the shared Grid to avoid ('prefer the shared Grid over a MaxHeight bound to the window height, because a window-relative MaxHeight still starves TopLevelPanel on short windows'), and a fixed pixel floor does exactly that. The new comment at MainWindow.xaml:39-41 says 'Every list then has a bounded height … and neither panel can push the other off the window', which is false across the lower part of the allowed height range. B-003 and B-007 run only at the default 880x600, so no case can see it. The builder's follow-up acknowledges the behaviour below the default, but the code comment claims the opposite, and nothing records a decision to accept it. This is a regression the merge carries into SL-039, whose results list got the rest of the window under a text-only outcome panel on uat. That last point is reasoned from uat's layout, not measured.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml:5 (MinHeight="400"), :39-41 (comment), :55 and :63 (MinHeight 316/328 on the outcome row); tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-B007 and Test-B003 (default window size only); measurements above.
findings.fix: Make the height range the window allows one where the floor fits, or make the floor yield. For the first, raise Window MinHeight to the smallest height at which all four of B-007's endings keep LargestFilesList, UnreadableList and TopLevelList in view; the measurements put that at roughly 550-600 px. For the second, derive the floor from the available height so the results row always keeps its header and one row. Either way, add a B-007 run at the window's MinHeight asserting that every list is inView, and correct the comment at :39-41. If choosing between a larger minimum window, tabs or a side-by-side layout needs a product decision, that is the window-size question already open for design-slice. Settle it there rather than leaving the comment claiming a guarantee the layout does not give.

drift: At the default 880x600 after an ending, SL-039's results list gets 31.26 px, or 19.26 px with the unreadable list open. That is less than one of its two-line rows. The builder declared it and the SL-039 doc now says so ('its header and part of a row'). Whether that is enough is part of the window-size question already open for design-slice, not something this review settles.

Not declared: the outcome row's floor applies even when the outcome needs less, because OutcomePanel is VerticalAlignment=Top in a row of at least 316 px. On a 2-file tree at 880x600 I measured OutcomePanel 211 px while TopLevelList stayed at 31.26 px, leaving about 105 px blank between the two panels. It is cosmetic, and it goes away with whatever the window-size decision settles.
